description:
Split out of fz-5xp.16 with authorization (user, 2026-09-07: 'we can skip them
for the moment').

`Enum.into/2,3` is the only Enum function that needs to put elements INTO
something without knowing what it is, and Elixir answers that with the
Collectable protocol -- a `into/1` callback returning an accumulator and a
command function that takes `{:cont, term}`, `:done` or `:halt`.

fz has protocols (String.Chars and Enumerable are two), so this is not new
machinery -- it is one more protocol plus impls for the collectable things fz
has: List, Map, and eventually String/binary.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING BEYOND into/2: Collectable is the OTHER HALF of
Enumerable, and fz has had only one half. Several Enum functions that currently
return lists because that is all they can build -- group_by, frequencies,
chunk_every -- would be able to build what the caller asked for.

Note fz's Enumerable already forks from Elixir's by carrying a fifth callback
(reduce_while/3). Adding Collectable is a good moment to decide whether that
fork stays, since it is the same design question about which callbacks a
protocol owes.
title: Enum.into/2,3 needs a Collectable protocol
